frontier.hypothesis: Class C closes if the RTL plus at insn 173 can be flipped to (shift, load) while the row-60 lw of D_800A36A0 stays a distinct in-place memory read. E4 proves both halves are individually reachable; nothing has yet obtained them together, and E4's only defect is the constant fold, not the order.
frontier.mechanism: Pointer-domain PLUS canonicalizes to (base, offset) and keeps the re-read (the floor-9 form); int-domain PLUS preserves written order but lets cse forward the loop-top `base` local's register, deleting the re-read and re-floating the p_6a/p_7e computation ahead of the 0x42/0x40/0x68 stores. E4 casts the SHIFT to u8 * so it becomes the canonical pointer operand while the global stays pointer-typed inside (s32)(D_800A36A0 + 0x6A) - the re-read survives - but 0x6A/0x7E then fold onto the shift operand before the add, turning one addu + two addiu into two addus (176 insns).
frontier.next_probe: Attack the CONSTANT FOLD, not the operand order. Keep the shift as the canonical pointer operand and force 0x6A/0x7E to stay on the RESULT of the add: e.g. give the two inner-loop pointers a common `(u8 *)(t0*10) + (s32)D_800A36A0`-shaped row whose two users each add their own constant afterwards, or index the row through a struct/array element type so +0x6A is a member offset rather than a folded addend. Read text1b.rtl (pre-optimization) for E4 (tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s6/v/E4.c) and for the baseline side by side to locate exactly where the fold happens; the baseline dump set is already in tmp/grind/func_800770B8/dumps/.
